text: Risk management is a key process for any project or business. It begins with identifying potential risks that could cause problems, such as delays, cost increases, or technical failures. Once these risks are known, teams develop mitigation strategies to reduce their likelihood or impact. For example, they might train staff, improve safety measures, or use more reliable materials. However, some risks may still occur, so it is important to have contingency plans in place. These are backup actions you take if a risk becomes a real issue. Finally, successful risk management requires continuous monitoring. By regularly reviewing the situation, you can spot new risks early and adjust your plans to stay prepared.
